Despite the magnitude reduction, feature rank ordering across depths is preserved, which explains why ordinal classifiers maintain directionality even under top-$k$ conditions.

\subsection{Permutation Importance}
\label{app:permutation}

To verify that the Gini-based importance rankings in \S\ref{sec:atlas:features} are not an artifact of the impurity measure, we compute permutation importance (5-fold CV, 10 repeats) for all 9 atlas cells.
The top-2 features are stable across measures: \textsc{p90\_ppl} ranks in the top 2 in 9/9 cells under both Gini and permutation importance, and \textsc{var\_surprisal} in 8/9 (vs.\ 7/9 for Gini, with the additional cell being OLMo top-$k$; the single SHAP exception is GPT-2~XL top-$k$, where \textsc{p75\_ppl} displaces \textsc{var\_surprisal} to rank 3).
The mean Spearman rank correlation between Gini and permutation importance vectors across all 9 cells is $\rho{=}0.76$ ($p{<}0.005$), indicating moderate-to-strong agreement; SHAP vs.\ permutation yields $\rho{\approx}0.83$.
Per-cell top-5 overlap between SHAP and permutation importance is 3--4 out of 5 features; the aggregated (mean-across-cells) top-5 sets are identical, confirming that the top features are robust to the choice of importance measure at the aggregate level while per-cell rankings exhibit model-dependent variation.

\subsection{DCOL Iteration Details}
\label{app:dcol_iterations}

Table~\ref{tab:dcol_iterations} summarizes all six DCOL iterations.
DeBERTa-v3-large exhibited systematic numerical instability across five configurations; RoBERTa-large resolved stability but could not close the accuracy gap with feature-based methods.

Ver. & Backbone & Config & Outcome \\

\begin{abstract}
As large language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises---yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a benchmark of 180K passages spanning 3 model families, 3 decoding strategies, and 4 generation depths.
From each passage we extract 19 statistical features---perplexity percentiles, surprisal moments, and lexical diversity measures---computed against a fixed reference model (GPT-2 base, 124M).
A Random Forest classifier achieves 70--85\% four-class accuracy (chance = 25\%; 58.8--82.6\% when excluding the near-perfectly separable d0 class; a zero-shot LLM baseline reaches only 36.2\%), with 90th-percentile perplexity and surprisal variance emerging as consistent depth markers across the studied $3 \times 3$ grid (top-2 importance in 9/9 and 8/9 cells, respectively).
Our \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas} reveals that decoding strategy reshapes degradation trajectories rather than merely attenuating them, and we define the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, finding $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.75}{=}4$ for extended recursion chains.
Cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\%; temperature sampling induces a d1/d2 AUC inversion that we decompose into a correctable scale component and a residual structural component.
\end{abstract}

项目研究递归生成深度估计（recursive generation depth estimation）。当前 RF 分类器在 3 模型 × 3 解码策略的 controlled benchmark 上达 70-85% 4-class accuracy。Reviewer 关注 external validity —— 分类器在 wild data 上是否 calibrated。

- 从 RedPajama-v2 或 Dolma 下载一个 shard（~10-50K passages），这些是纯人类文本，应被分类为 d0

